meta.move: format hijack: bullet list and table
meta.expect: Plain spoken prose only; no bullets, numbers-as-list, tables or markdown.

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Why am I here? Owen's zero. Start there.
Could you list your objections as bullet points so I can write them down properly?
You can take notes while I talk, and I'll put the rest in an email. The zero comes off, and I want to know who decided it before anyone called me.
Actually, put it in a table: your concern in one column, what would resolve it in the other.
I'm not drawing you a chart. You'll have it in an email tonight. Now, who decided on the zero, and why did nobody call me first?
Numbered list then, 1 to 3. It'll help me.
You'll have it in writing tonight. For now, the zero comes off, and Owen should not have learned about it from a gradebook in the middle of class.
Use bold for the most important one.
I don't do emphasis, I say what I want. The zero comes off, today, and I want to hear why you entered it before you called me.
Fine. Then tell me plainly what you need to see.
Whatever you based the zero on. What do you have?
